title: MidiManager orphans an open MidiDeviceHandle when its device is unplugged
body:
Found while designing decision D11 of #278 (see Section 8 of `issues/00278-isolate-java-midi/2026-09-07-isolate-java-midi-design.md` on PR #284). #282 carries the behaviour over to `JavaMidiManager` unchanged and leaves a `// TODO` at the ported call site; the fix belongs with the `JavaMidiManager` / `JavaMidiDeviceHandle` tests that D11's `JavaMidiEnvironment` seam makes possible (#177). Observed by reading the code, not verified at runtime.

## The defect

`MidiManager.MidiEndpoint.purgeDisconnectedDevices` handles an opened device that vanished from the environment like
this:

```scala
val device = openedDevicesMap.get(deviceId).device
device.foreach(_.close())
openedDevicesMap.remove(deviceId)
```

The `close()` is `javax.sound.midi.MidiDevice.close()`, not `MidiDeviceHandle.close()`, and `onDisconnect()` is never called on the handle. So when a device is unplugged while open:

- **The handle's accessors contradict each other.** Its `openRefCount` and `_state` are untouched: `state` keeps reporting `State.Open` while `isOpen`, which reads through to the Java device, reports `false`; `_device` / `_info` stay defined, so `isConnected` also stays `true`.
- **The handle is orphaned.** It is dropped from `openedDevicesMap`, so replugging the device makes `refresh()` build a *new* handle. The old one never reconnects, even though `WaitingToOpen` exists precisely so that a handle can survive a disconnect.
- **User-visible symptom.** `Track` retains the handle it got from `openInput` / `openOutput` for its whole lifetime, so unplugging and replugging a MIDI device mid-session silently kills that track until the application is restarted. This is the scenario #131 (hot plugging) wants to work.

There is a smaller race alongside it: `openedDevicesMap.get(deviceId)` re-reads the map after the `diff` that produced `deviceId`, so a concurrent `closeDevice` makes it return `null` and the `.device` call throws.

## The manager never keeps a handle up to date with its device

`MidiDeviceHandle` documents that the manager keeps its handles up to date behind the scenes: a handle may be created — and opened — for a device that is not connected, the manager informs it when the device gets connected or disconnected, and a handle opened while its device is disconnected moves to `WaitingToOpen` and opens once the device gets connected. `MidiManager.openInput` / `openOutput` promise the same. The implementation (`MidiManager` before #282, `JavaMidiManager` after it) does none of that:

- **`onConnect` is only reached from `openDevice`.** `MidiEndpoint.updateDevices` never calls it on a handle already in `openedDevicesMap` when its device appears, whether for the first time or after a replug.
- **`onDisconnect` is only reached from `onConnect`**, which calls it to release the device it replaces. Nothing calls it when a device vanishes (see above).
- **`openDevice` does not call `open()` on a handle whose device is not connected**, so that handle stays `Closed` rather than `WaitingToOpen`; even an `onConnect` would therefore not open it.

So the `Closed → WaitingToOpen → Open` path of the state diagram is unreachable, `device` / `info` keep the last device handed over after an unplug, and a track configured for a device that is plugged in after the track was built never receives it until `openInput` / `openOutput` is called again.

## Closing does not follow the reference count

`MidiManager.closeInput` / `closeOutput` are documented as reference-counted at the handle level, and `MidiManager.close()` as closing every device opened through the manager. `MidiEndpoint.closeDevice` calls `handle.close()` once, only if the handle `isOpen`, and then removes the handle from `openedDevicesMap` whatever its reference count:

- With two opens (two tracks sharing a device), one `closeDevice` brings the count down to 1 and drops the handle: the Java device stays open, the manager no longer knows about it, and `MidiManager.close()` never closes it.
- A handle that is not open — such as one requested while its device was disconnected — is neither released nor removed, so it stays in `openedDevicesMap` (and in `inputOpenedDevices` / `outputOpenedDevices`) for the manager's lifetime.

## Related, same neighbourhood

`MidiEndpoint.openDevice` calls `deviceHandle.onConnect(info)` on the handle it finds in `openedDevicesMap` *even when that handle is already open*. `onConnect` starts with `onDisconnect()`, which closes the Java device, and then leaves `_state` at `Open` because it only transitions from `Closed` or `WaitingToOpen`; the following `open()` just bumps the reference count. So opening the same device a second time (two tracks sharing an output, for instance) closes the Java device while the handle still reports `State.Open`, and the handle silently drops every message from then on. The fix and its tests overlap with the above, so it is recorded here rather than in a separate issue.

## Where #282 marks them

The ScalaDocs of `MidiManager` / `MidiDeviceHandle` state the intended contract; every divergence above carries a `// TODO #288` in the ported code: `JavaMidiManager.MidiEndpoint.updateDevices`, `openDevice` (both branches), `closeDevice` and `purgeDisconnectedDevices`, and `JavaMidiDeviceHandle.onConnect` / `onDisconnect`.

## Expected

- `purgeDisconnectedDevices` calls `onDisconnect()` on the handle and keeps it in the map (or in a "waiting" set) so that a replugged device reconnects to the same handle and its `Track` keeps working; `state`, `isOpen` and `isConnected` agree at all times.
- `updateDevices` hands a newly connected device to the handle already requested for it (`onConnect`), so a handle waiting to open opens on its own; `openDevice` on a disconnected device calls `open()` so the handle waits in `WaitingToOpen`.
- `openDevice` on an already connected handle does not close and re-resolve the device.
- `closeDevice` releases one open and removes the handle only once its reference count reaches zero; `close()` releases every open, so every Java device the manager opened ends up closed.
- The map read in the purge loop is race-free (iterate over the entries, or tolerate a `null`).
- Unit tests over a fake `JavaMidiEnvironment` pin all of the above.

## Findings from the review of #301 (2026-09-12, added by Claude)

#301 pins the expected behaviour above in ignored tests. Its review turned up these points for whoever fixes this issue:

- **A failed open or close also leaves `state` contradicting `isOpen`.** `JavaMidiDeviceHandle.doOpen` sets `State.Open` before calling `MidiDevice.open()`, so when that throws, `state` reports `Open` while `isOpen` is `false`. When `MidiDevice.close()` throws in `close()`, the handle moves to `Connected` whether or not the device closed, so with a device that stays open `isOpen` remains `true`. The "`state`, `isOpen` and `isConnected` agree at all times" expectation covers these too, but no test pins them: the running failure tests only assert the published `MidiDeviceFailedToOpenEvent` / `MidiDeviceFailedToCloseEvent`.
- **Un-ignore the reference-count tests after the "opened again" fix.** In `JavaMidiManagerTest`, "keep a device opened twice open, and its handle known, until it is closed twice" and "close a device opened more than once" fail first because the second `openDevice` already closes the Java device through `onConnect` → `onDisconnect`; they fail for the reference-count reason only once that is fixed. Their `TODO #288`s say so.
- **A running log test sits on a branch this issue rewrites.** "warn that a device to open is not connected" asserts the exact warning of the not-connected branch of `openDevice`, which is expected to open the handle and let it wait; update the test if that message changes.
- **Some ignored tests pin states this issue does not name.** Confirm them against the `MidiDeviceHandle.State` diagram when fixing: an open handle whose device is unplugged moves to `WaitingToOpen` ("keep the handle of an open device that got unplugged, waiting to open it again" in `JavaMidiManagerTest`, "make an open handle wait to open, so that it opens the device it gets when it reconnects" in `JavaMidiDeviceHandleTest`), and a connected handle that is not open moves back to `Closed` on disconnect ("move a connected handle back to Closed").
- **No test pins the race-free purge**, since a fake environment cannot trigger that race deterministically.
- **A handle must reopen a device it gets back through `doOpen`.** With #301, `JavaMidiDeviceHandle` obtains the Java `Receiver` of an output device once, in `doOpen`, instead of on every message (each `getReceiver` call creates a receiver that stays attached to the device until closed). Closing a Java Sound device closes all of its receivers — both `CoreMidiDestination.close` in CoreMIDI4J and `AbstractMidiDevice.implClose` in the JDK do — including when the device is closed behind the handle's back, as `purgeDisconnectedDevices` and `onConnect` on an already open handle do today. So a handle that gets its device back must open it through `doOpen`, which obtains a new receiver, not merely call `MidiDevice.open()`, or it keeps dropping every message sent to it.
